comment: SNOMED product and licence distinctions — The existing “representative subset” wording does not tell readers which semantic capabilities they actually receive. This correction should not be used to claim that GPS is only a demonstration product or that free IPS terminology is unavailable. Evidence: GPS (https://www.snomed.org/gps), IPS Terminology overview (https://docs.snomed.org/implementation-guides/snomed-ips-terminology-implementation-guide/2-ips-terminology-overview).

public.suggestedRevision: Replace whole footnote: *Implementers should distinguish full SNOMED CT, the Global Patient Set (GPS), and SNOMED International's IPS Terminology and check the terms and capabilities of the actual product and release used. GPS provides identifiers, selected English names, and status information, but excludes the relationships and hierarchies of full SNOMED CT. IPS Terminology is a separate, more limited clinical-content product with its own scope. Free access to one product does not imply that it supplies the functionality or usage rights of another. ICD-11 content and WHO software also have published terms of use; see the Terminology Service licensing requirements.*
